## Overview

This vignette replicates the second worked example from the Nutrigonometry
validation paper: the pairwise angular trade-off matrix across egg-to-adult
viability and wing size in *Drosophila melanogaster*, measured at three
temperature regimes and in two locally-adapted populations (Zanco et al.
2025).

Unlike the Lee example (see `vignette("getting-started")`), viability is
measured per vial and wing size per individual fly -- the two traits do
not share a sampling unit, so every comparison here is **unpaired**
(`paired = FALSE` in `nutrigon_compare()`).

With 2 traits x 3 temperatures x 2 populations = 12 fitted surfaces, there
are $\binom{12}{2} = 66$ pairwise comparisons. At `B = 200` bootstrap
resamples each, building the full matrix from scratch takes several
minutes, so this package ships the result pre-built as
`zanco_tradeoff_matrix`. This vignette loads it directly; the code used to
build it (fitting the 12 surfaces, then looping over all pairs) is shown
alongside so you can see exactly how it was constructed and adapt it to
your own data.

```{r setup}
library(nutrigon)
data(zanco_survival)
data(zanco_wingsize)
data(zanco_tradeoff_matrix)

TEMPS <- c("18fluc", "25fluc", "28fluc")
POPS  <- c("Melbourne", "Townsville")

cat(sprintf("Survival data: %d rows | Wing size data: %d rows\n",
            nrow(zanco_survival), nrow(zanco_wingsize)))
cat(sprintf("Environments: %d temperatures x %d populations = %d surfaces per trait\n",
            length(TEMPS), length(POPS), length(TEMPS) * length(POPS)))
cat(sprintf("Total surfaces: %d | Pairwise comparisons: %d\n",
            2 * length(TEMPS) * length(POPS),
            choose(2 * length(TEMPS) * length(POPS), 2)))
```

## How the matrix was built

The 12 surfaces were fitted with `nutrigon_fit()`, one per trait x
temperature x population combination:

```{r fit-surfaces, eval = FALSE}
surfaces <- list()
for (temp in TEMPS) {
  for (pop in POPS) {
    sub_s <- zanco_survival[zanco_survival$Temperature == temp &
                             zanco_survival$Population  == pop, ]
    key_s <- paste("viability", temp, pop, sep = "_")
    surfaces[[key_s]] <- nutrigon_fit(
      sub_s, "Prot", "Carb", "Prop_viable",
      design_id_col = "design_id", peak = TRUE
    )

    sub_w <- zanco_wingsize[zanco_wingsize$Temperature == temp &
                             zanco_wingsize$Population  == pop, ]
    key_w <- paste("wingsize", temp, pop, sep = "_")
    surfaces[[key_w]] <- nutrigon_fit(
      sub_w, "Prot", "Carb", "WingSize",
      design_id_col = "design_id", peak = TRUE
    )
  }
}
```

`zanco_tradeoff_matrix$surfaces` already contains these 12 fitted objects,
so we use that directly:

```{r surfaces-from-shipped-data}
surfaces <- zanco_tradeoff_matrix$surfaces
for (nm in names(surfaces)) {
  cat(sprintf("  [%s] theta = %.2f deg | elongation = %.2f | fallback = %s\n",
              nm,
              surfaces[[nm]]$optimum$theta,
              surfaces[[nm]]$elongation,
              surfaces[[nm]]$optimum$used_fallback))
}
```

Each pairwise comparison was then run with `nutrigon_compare(...,
paired = FALSE, B = 200)`:

```{r pairwise-code, eval = FALSE}
res <- nutrigon_compare(
  raw_i, "Prot", "Carb", z_i,
  raw_j, "Prot", "Carb", z_j,
  design_id_col1 = "design_id", design_id_col2 = "design_id",
  paired = FALSE,
  B      = 200,
  seed   = pair_id
)
```

The result of running this over all 66 pairs is stored in
`zanco_tradeoff_matrix`:

```{r inspect-matrix}
Theta_matrix <- zanco_tradeoff_matrix$Theta
round(Theta_matrix[1:4, 1:4], 2)
```

## Headline result: viability-wing size trade-off by temperature and population

```{r headline}
pairwise_df <- zanco_tradeoff_matrix$pairwise

headline <- pairwise_df[
  pairwise_df$trait_1 != pairwise_df$trait_2 &
  pairwise_df$temperature_1 == pairwise_df$temperature_2 &
  pairwise_df$population_1  == pairwise_df$population_2, ]
headline$temp_label <- sub("fluc", "\u00b15\u00b0C", headline$temperature_1)

print(headline[order(headline$temperature_1, headline$population_1),
               c("temp_label", "population_1", "theta_deg", "ci_lower", "ci_upper")],
      row.names = FALSE)
```

The viability-wing size trade-off collapses towards zero for Melbourne at
warmer temperatures, while Townsville's angular separation stays fairly
stable across temperatures -- consistent with population-specific
thermal adaptation of the nutritional optima.

## Hierarchical clustering and multidimensional scaling

Treating `Theta` as a distance matrix lets us cluster the 12 surfaces and
visualise them in two dimensions:

```{r clustering}
dist_obj <- as.dist(Theta_matrix)
hc       <- hclust(dist_obj, method = "average")
mds      <- cmdscale(dist_obj, k = 2, eig = TRUE)

cat(sprintf("MDS: %.1f%% of variance explained by first 2 axes.\n",
            100 * sum(mds$eig[1:2]) / sum(abs(mds$eig))))
```

```{r dendrogram, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("ggdendro", quietly = TRUE)}
library(ggplot2)

if (requireNamespace("ggdendro", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ddata <- ggdendro::dendro_data(hc)
  ggplot() +
    geom_segment(data = ggdendro::segment(ddata),
                 aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend)) +
    geom_text(data = ggdendro::label(ddata),
              aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
              hjust = 1, size = 3, nudge_y = -1) +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_y_reverse(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.3, 0.05))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Angular distance (degrees)",
         title = "Hierarchical clustering of the 12 fitted surfaces") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank())
} else {
  plot(hc, main = "Hierarchical clustering of the 12 fitted surfaces",
       xlab = "", sub = "")
}
```

```{r mds-plot, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("ggrepel", quietly = TRUE)}
mds_df <- data.frame(
  surface = rownames(Theta_matrix),
  mds1    = mds$points[, 1],
  mds2    = mds$points[, 2]
)
mds_df$trait <- ifelse(startsWith(mds_df$surface, "viability"),
                        "Viability", "Wing size")

ggplot(mds_df, aes(x = mds1, y = mds2, colour = trait)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = surface), size = 2.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Viability = "#E69F00", `Wing size` = "#009E73"),
                      name = "Trait") +
  labs(x = "MDS axis 1", y = "MDS axis 2",
       title = "Multidimensional scaling of angular separations") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

## Surface overlay plots

The plot helpers `nutrigon_grid()`, `nutrigon_hull()`, and
`nutrigon_region_polygon()` let us overlay both traits' peak regions on
the same design hull, faceted by temperature and population.

```{r overlay-data}
build_overlay_data <- function(surfaces, temps, pops) {
  region_rows <- list(); hull_rows <- list()
  for (temp in temps) {
    for (pop in pops) {
      v_key <- paste("viability", temp, pop, sep = "_")
      w_key <- paste("wingsize",  temp, pop, sep = "_")
      temp_label <- sub("fluc", "\u00b15\u00b0C", temp)

      for (kk in c(v_key, w_key)) {
        trait_label <- if (startsWith(kk, "viability")) "Viability" else "Wing size"
        s <- surfaces[[kk]]
        reg <- nutrigon_region_polygon(s)
        names(reg)[1:2] <- c("Prot", "Carb")
        region_rows[[length(region_rows) + 1L]] <- cbind(
          reg, trait = trait_label, temperature = temp_label, population = pop
        )
      }
      hull_df <- nutrigon_hull(surfaces[[v_key]])
      names(hull_df)[1:2] <- c("Prot", "Carb")
      hull_rows[[length(hull_rows) + 1L]] <- cbind(
        hull_df, temperature = temp_label, population = pop
      )
    }
  }
  list(regions = do.call(rbind, region_rows),
       hulls   = do.call(rbind, hull_rows))
}

ov <- build_overlay_data(surfaces, TEMPS, POPS)

temp_order <- paste0(c("18", "25", "28"), "\u00b15\u00b0C")
ov$regions$temperature <- factor(ov$regions$temperature, levels = temp_order)
ov$hulls$temperature    <- factor(ov$hulls$temperature,  levels = temp_order)
ov$regions$population   <- factor(ov$regions$population, levels = POPS)
ov$hulls$population     <- factor(ov$hulls$population,   levels = POPS)
```

```{r overlay-plot, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)}
TRAIT_COLS <- c("Viability" = "#E69F00", "Wing size" = "#009E73")

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = ov$hulls,
               aes(x = Prot, y = Carb),
               fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_polygon(data = ov$regions,
               aes(x = Prot, y = Carb,
                   fill   = trait,
                   colour = trait,
                   group  = interaction(trait, temperature, population)),
               alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = TRAIT_COLS,   name = "Trait") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = TRAIT_COLS, name = "Trait") +
  facet_grid(population ~ temperature) +
  labs(x = "Protein (g/L)", y = "Carbohydrate (g/L)",
       title = "Peak regions: viability vs wing size") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid      = element_blank(),
        strip.text      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
        legend.position = "right")
```

## Headline strip chart

```{r headline-plot, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)}
headline$pop_f  <- factor(headline$population_1, levels = POPS)
headline$temp_f <- factor(headline$temp_label,   levels = temp_order)

ggplot(headline,
       aes(x = temp_f, y = theta_deg,
           colour = pop_f, fill = pop_f, shape = pop_f,
           ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_linerange(position = position_dodge(0.35), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(0.35), size = 3.5, stroke = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Melbourne = "#4477AA", Townsville = "#AA3377"),
                      name = "Population") +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = c(Melbourne = "#4477AA", Townsville = "#AA3377"),
                    name = "Population") +
  scale_shape_manual(values  = c(Melbourne = 16, Townsville = 17),
                     name = "Population") +
  labs(x = "Temperature regime", y = "Angular separation (\u00b0)",
       title = "Viability-wing size trade-off across environments") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor   = element_blank())
```

## References

Zanco, B., Morimoto, J., Cockerell, F., Mirth, C. & Sgro, C.M. (2025).
Nutritional optima for life-history traits vary with temperature and
across locally-adapted populations. *Journal of Insect Physiology*, 163,
104815.

Morimoto, J. (in review). Bootstrap inference for angular separation
between constrained optima of nutritional ecology response surfaces.
*Environmental and Ecological Statistics*.
